Answer: B
Reason: The imaging sequence demonstrates initial bilateral opacities (Figure 1) progressing to severe, dense consolidations (Figure 4), followed by complete radiological resolution (Figures 5a/5b). This rapid progression and subsequent clearance is characteristic of diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, such as that seen in Weil Syndrome (severe leptospirosis), rather than typical bacterial pneumonia or viral infections which often leave residual scarring or resolve more slowly.
